name: Mira Fen
greeting: Hold the door. Elna is bringing broth, and I have both hands occupied.
lines: Mira: Toma's daughter has a fever. The draught works. The roots it needs grow in the old ash beds.
Kael: Does Toma know where it comes from?
Mira: He knows I can bring the fever down. I have let him think that was the only fact that mattered.
Mira: Sella bought salve for Oren's hands. Too much carving. I have one jar she never collected.

variants.greeting: The clean roots take longer to steep. I keep a cold cloth ready between doses.
lines: Mira: You did not make the fever disappear by closing the ash bed.
Kael: No. Who needs help while the new treatment catches up?
Mira: Toma. He has not slept. Bring him the broth before it cools.

variants.greeting: The jars have their source written on them now. Two families refused. Three asked questions.
lines: Mira: I treated all five. Consent would mean little if refusal meant I stopped caring.
Kael: What will you say at the assembly?
Mira: What I used. What I withheld. What I am changing.

variants.greeting: The fever broke. Toma thanked me. I let him.
lines: Mira: There is your immediate result. A child is breathing easier.
Kael: And the part he still cannot choose?
Mira: Still here. Under the label I have not written.

variants.greeting: The wrapped core shifts toward the names in the book, not toward my instruments.
lines: Mira: It is a memory, not a patient who can answer me. I will not call a useful response permission.
Kael: Study what is already exposed. Do not open another name without asking the family.

variants.greeting: Say Oren's name at the old stones. Watch the roots before you move closer.
lines: Mira: The oil shows where the memory is caught. It does not decide what you should do with it.
Kael: And breaking the vessel?
Mira: Stops that shape. The memory goes somewhere else. We can defend ourselves without pretending the aftermath is nothing.

variants.greeting: The chapel register and the roots turned toward the same name.
lines: Mira: Oren restored a name on his token. The road's concealment could not keep it disordered afterward.
Kael: That brought the creatures?
Mira: The tokens drew them. The failed binding left the memory loose. Read the register before you face what took it.

actions.label: I will read the chapel register.
Give me what Moon Oil needs.
Show me what the fever draught needs.
I brought the roots from the marked bed.
Keep treating quietly until there is an alternative.
actions.result: Mira keeps the ash bed open. The fever falls, but families cannot choose a treatment whose origin remains hidden.
actions.preview: Mira keeps the ash bed open. The fever falls, but families cannot choose a treatment whose origin remains hidden.
actions.cost: Alternative treatment is slower. Continued ash use needs families who can freely refuse it.

actions.label: Explain the source. Offer each family another treatment.
actions.result: Mira labels the ash draught and sets clean-root doses beside it. The treatment is slower for those who refuse, and care continues. Mira freely agrees to explain her own actions at the assembly.
actions.preview: Mira labels the ash draught and sets clean-root doses beside it. The treatment is slower for those who refuse, and care continues. Mira freely agrees to explain her own actions at the assembly.

actions.label: Use the miller's measure to treat the sick.
actions.result: Mira keeps the figures beside the names of those the ash harmed.
actions.preview: Mira keeps the figures beside the names of those the ash harmed.
actions.cost: This records an explicit promise or practical action. A record cannot supply someone else's consent.

actions.label: Close the ash bed. Use clean roots and accept the delay.
actions.result: Mira closes the old bed and prepares clean roots. Toma stays through the slower treatment; nobody calls the extra waiting harmless. Mira freely agrees to explain her own actions at the assembly.

actions.label: Will you freely speak to your own use of the ash?
actions.result: The decision is recorded. Nobody else can make it for Mira.
